mainTopic: Collecting from תם oxen when it is unclear which ox did the damage, and how to divide payment when one ox gores several oxen in a row
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion: the ניזק is 'fitting to take' payment, but in practice he gets nothing unless he already seized the ox. Then the גמרא turns to the משנה's line that if both chasing oxen belong to one owner, both are liable. רבא מפרזיקא wants to learn from this that with תם oxen the ניזק can collect from either ox. רב אשי says the משנה is about מועד oxen, and then splits the משנה between the two kinds of oxen. רב אחא סבא shows from the wording 'חייבים' and 'שניהם' that the oxen must be תמין. The גמרא concludes that the משנה follows רבי עקיבא, who makes the ניזק a partner, and that the rule applies only while both oxen are present. פרק המניח ends, and a new משנה describes an ox that gored several oxen one after another, with רבי מאיר's and רבי שמעון's ways of dividing the payment. The גמרא asks whose view this משנה follows: it does not fit רבי ישמעאל, and the challenge from רבי עקיבא's view continues on the next amud.

steps.title: He deserves payment but does not actually get it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers an earlier question. The משנה does not mean the ניזק really collects. It only means he would have been entitled to collect.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is fitting for him to take, but he does not have anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer from the previous discussion. The ניזק would have deserved payment, but in practice he walks away with nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא was bothered that the משנה seemed to let the ניזק collect, even though the only version he could collect on was the מזיק's admission, which the ניזק himself denied. The answer separates two ideas: being entitled in principle, and actually collecting in court. The משנה is only describing the first.

keyTerms.meaning: fitting / entitled to take
but he has nothing (he does not actually collect)
the injured party (owner of the damaged animal)

phrases.english: It is fitting for him to take, but he does not have [anything].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question raised before this section begins.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the משנה's wording: entitlement, not actual collection.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say the ניזק actually collects.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ניזק is only theoretically entitled. In practice he gets nothing.

steps.title: A ברייתא says he does get paid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer with a ברייתא that says the ניזק is paid: for his small ox from the מועד, and for his large ox from the תם.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: he is paid for the small one from the מועד, and for the large one from the תם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It brings a ברייתא that clearly says the ניזק receives payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 said the ניזק gets nothing. This ברייתא uses the active word 'משתלם', meaning he is paid. That sounds like real collection, which contradicts 'ואין לו'.

keyTerms.meaning: receives payment
an ox with an established record of goring; pays full damage
an ox with no record of goring; pays half damage, only from its own body

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: הֲרֵי זֶה מִשְׁתַּלֵּם לַקָּטָן מִן הַמּוּעָד,
phrases.english: But it was taught: this one is paid for the small one from the forewarned [ox],
phrases.notes: 'The small one' and 'the large one' here are the ניזק's own injured oxen.

phrases.english: and for the large one from the innocuous [ox]!

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ניזק is entitled but receives nothing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says outright that he receives payment, so 'ואין לו' cannot be right.

steps.title: The ברייתא is a case where he already grabbed the ox
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a case where the ניזק already seized the ox. In that case the court lets him keep what he took.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with one word. The ברייתא is a case where the ניזק had already grabbed the animal himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court will not force payment out of the owner from the start. But if the ניזק already holds the animal, the court does not take it away from him. So 'משתלם' in the ברייתא means he gets to keep it, and both sources fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: seizing; 'where he seized' the item himself

steps.whatToRemember: The ניזק is entitled but cannot get the court to make the owner pay. If he already seized the ox, he keeps it.

phrases.english: Where he seized [it].
phrases.notes: The ניזק took hold of the animal before coming to court, so he gets to keep it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a specific case (seizure).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means the court actually makes the owner pay.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only where the ניזק already seized the ox, so it matches 'ואין לו'.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: both oxen of one owner are liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. If both chasing oxen belong to one person, both are liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: If both belonged to one person, both are liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line of the משנה. It is setting up the next move, an inference about how payment is collected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is two oxen chasing a third, where we don't know which one did the damage. When the same person owns both oxen, the משנה says both are 'liable'. The next step asks what that word implies.

keyTerms.meaning: both are liable
one person (a single owner)

phrases.english: If both of them belonged to one person –
both are liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When one owner has both oxen, both oxen are liable for the damage.

steps.title: Inference: with תם oxen he may collect from either one
steps.stepSummary: רבא מפרזיקא suggests to רב אשי a lesson from the משנה. When תם oxen cause damage, the ניזק can collect from whichever ox he chooses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא מפרזיקא said to רב אשי: Learn from this that if תם oxen caused damage, he may collect from this one or from that one, as he wishes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא מפרזיקא draws a conclusion from the משנה. If both oxen are liable, then the ניזק can take his payment from either ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a תם pays only from its own body, so you would need to know which ox did it. Since the משנה makes both liable, it seems the ניזק can pick either ox to collect from. This would be a new rule about תם oxen.

keyTerms.meaning: רבא of the town Parzika, an אמורא
learn from this (introduces an inference)
collects (payment)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא מִפַּרְזִיקָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rava of Parzika said to Rav Ashi:
Learn from this: innocuous oxen that caused damage –

phrases.aramaic: רָצָה מִזֶּה גּוֹבֶה, רָצָה מִזֶּה גּוֹבֶה.
phrases.english: if he wishes, he collects from this one; if he wishes, he collects from that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the משנה line quoted in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: With תם oxen, the ניזק may collect from whichever ox he chooses.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that both oxen of one owner are liable.

steps.title: No: the משנה is about מועד oxen
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects the inference. The משנה is talking about מועד oxen, which pay from all the owner's property, so it teaches nothing about תם oxen.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? With מועד oxen.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back. He says the משנה is about מועד oxen, so you cannot learn a rule about תם oxen from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מועד pays full damage from any of the owner's property, not only from the ox itself. So naturally the ניזק can collect from either ox. That tells us nothing about תם oxen, which pay only from their own body.

keyTerms.meaning: with what case are we dealing here? (limits a source to a specific case)

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here? With forewarned [oxen].
phrases.notes: This is רב אשי answering רבא מפרזיקא.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof, not necessarily the rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the משנה is about תם oxen, but it may be about מועד oxen.

steps.title: The סיפא shows the oxen must be תם
steps.stepSummary: רבא מפרזיקא challenges רב אשי from the סיפא. The משנה has the two sides arguing over which ox did the damage, and puts the burden of proof on the ניזק. With מועד oxen that argument would make no difference, because full damage is paid either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they are מועד, look at the סיפא: one was large and one small. The ניזק says the large one did the damage, and the מזיק says, 'No, the small one did.' The one who wants to take from his fellow must bring proof. But if they are מועד, what difference does it make to him? In the end he has to pay the value of a full ox!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא מפרזיקא attacks רב אשי's answer. He quotes the end of the משנה, where the two sides argue over which ox did it. That argument only makes sense if the oxen are תם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a מועד, the owner pays full damage from all his property, so it does not matter whether the large or small ox did it. With a תם, payment comes only from the body of that ox, so which ox did it matters a great deal. Since the משנה treats the question as important, it must be talking about תם oxen.

keyTerms.meaning: look at the latter part (of the משנה)
whoever wants to take from another must bring proof
what difference does it make to him?
in the end, either way
a full, complete ox (full damage value)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Large' and 'small' here describe the oxen that did the damage, not the injured oxen as in step 2. This matters because a small תם ox's body may not be worth enough to cover the damage.
steps.whyThisMatters: This puts רב אשי's answer in question and keeps open the possibility that the משנה is about תם oxen. It is a classic move: using the סיפא to show what case the whole משנה must be about.

phrases.english: If [it is] with forewarned [oxen], say the latter clause:
If one was large and one small,
the injured party says: "The large one caused the damage,"

phrases.aramaic: וְהַמַּזִּיק אוֹמֵר: ״לֹא כִי, אֶלָּא קָטָן הִזִּיק״ –
phrases.english: and the one liable says: "Not so, rather the small one caused the damage" –
the one who takes from his fellow bears the burden of proof.

phrases.aramaic: אִי בְּמוּעָדִין, מַאי נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִינֵּיהּ?
phrases.english: If [it is] with forewarned [oxen], what difference does it make to him?
Ultimately,
he must pay the value of a full ox!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's answer in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that the משנה is about מועד oxen.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא treats 'which ox did it' as a real dispute needing proof. With מועד oxen that would make no difference, so the משנה must be about תם oxen.

steps.title: רב אשי splits the משנה between the two kinds of oxen
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the סיפא of the משנה is about תמין oxen, while the רישא is about מועדין oxen.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The last part of the משנה is about תמין oxen, and the first part is about מועדין oxen.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends himself against רבא מפרזיקא's challenge. He says the two parts of the משנה are talking about different kinds of oxen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא מפרזיקא argued that the סיפא, where they argue over which ox did the damage, only makes sense with תמין oxen. רב אשי agrees about the סיפא but keeps his reading of the רישא as מועדין. That way the רישא still teaches nothing about collecting from תמין oxen.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of a משנה or ברייתא
The opening part of a משנה or ברייתא
Oxen with no record of goring; the owner pays half damages, and only from the ox itself
Oxen with a record of goring; the owner pays full damages from all his property

phrases.english: He said to him: The latter clause is about innocuous oxen,
phrases.notes: The speaker is רב אשי, answering רבא מפרזיקא's challenge from the previous step.

phrases.english: and the first clause is about forewarned oxen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: סֵיפָא בְּתַמִּין, וְרֵישָׁא בְּמוּעָדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7 by giving the רישא and the סיפא different cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Split case (אוקימתא): the two clauses deal with different kinds of oxen
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole משנה deals with one kind of ox, so the סיפא proves the רישא is about תמין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא is about תמין and the רישא is about מועדין, so the רישא still teaches nothing about תמין.

steps.title: The משנה's wording does not fit forewarned oxen
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא סבא challenges רב אשי: if the רישא were about מועדין, the משנה should have said the man is liable, not 'they are liable.' And why would it say 'both'?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא סבא said to רב אשי: If it is about מועדין oxen, why does it say 'they are liable'? It should have said 'the man is liable'! And also, what does 'both of them' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא, רב אחא סבא, attacks רב אשי's answer using the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With מועדין oxen, the owner pays from all his property, so it is really the person who is liable, not the oxen. The plural 'חייבים' and the word 'שניהם' point to the two oxen themselves being liable. That only makes sense with תמין oxen, where payment comes from the ox's body.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They are liable' (plural), pointing to the two oxen
The man, meaning the owner himself
'Both of them', the two oxen
'And furthermore', adding a second challenge

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא סָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha the Elder said to Rav Ashi:
If it is about forewarned oxen, 'they are liable'?!
It should have said 'the man is liable'!
And furthermore, what is 'both of them'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 8, which said the רישא is about מועדין.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that the רישא of the משנה is about מועדין oxen
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plural 'חייבים' and the word 'שניהם' describe the oxen as liable. That fits תמין, which pay from the ox's body, not מועדין, where the owner pays.

steps.title: Both clauses are about innocuous oxen, following רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא retracts. The רישא is also about תמין, following רבי עקיבא, who says the ניזק becomes a partner in the ox. The ניזק can take either ox only when both oxen are still there; otherwise the owner can demand proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה really is about תמין oxen, and it follows רבי עקיבא, who says the ניזק and the owner are partners in the ox. The reason both are liable is that both oxen are there, so the owner cannot push the ניזק away. But if both are not there, the owner can say: 'Go bring proof that this ox damaged you, and I will pay you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the idea that the רישא is about מועדין and gives a new explanation. It also limits when the ניזק can collect from either ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי עקיבא, once a תם gores, the ניזק becomes a partner in that ox. When both oxen are standing there and both belong to the owner, he cannot put the ניזק off, so both are liable. If one of them is gone, the owner can demand proof of which ox did the damage. So the rule only works when both oxen are present.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Actually', returning to an earlier possibility
Partners; the ניזק becomes part-owner of the ox that damaged him
To push off or put off a claimant
Proof

steps.whatToRemember: Two תמין oxen of one owner that chased and damaged are both liable, following רבי עקיבא, but only while both oxen are still there. If one is gone, the ניזק must prove which ox did the damage.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ניזק can always collect from whichever ox he wants. That works only when both oxen are present.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers both challenges at once. The wording 'חייבים, שניהם' fits תמין, and the סיפא's argument over proof fits too, because proof matters once one ox is no longer there.

phrases.english: Rather, it is actually about innocuous oxen;
and it follows Rabbi Akiva, who says:
they are partners;
phrases.notes: He means the injured party and the owner share ownership of the ox that did the damage.

phrases.english: and the reason is that both of them are there –
so he cannot push him off,
but if both of them are not there –
he can say to him:

phrases.aramaic: זִיל אַיְיתִי רְאָיָה דְּהַאי תּוֹרָא אַזְּקָךְ,
phrases.english: Go bring proof that this ox damaged you,
and I will pay you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְעוֹלָם בְּתַמִּין; וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the קשיא of step 9 and replaces רב אשי's split with a new reading of the whole משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction and new אוקימתא: the רישא is about תמין, following רבי עקיבא, and limited to when both oxen are present
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רישא is about מועדין (step 8), or it shows that the ניזק can always collect from either תם ox (step 5).
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא is about תמין, following רבי עקיבא. Both oxen are liable only when both are present; otherwise the ניזק must bring proof.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק המניח
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the third פרק of בבא קמא, פרק המניח.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק המניח.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument. It is the traditional line said when finishing a פרק, and it marks the end of פרק המניח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line expresses the learner's wish to come back to this פרק again. The next line of text opens a new פרק with a new משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you', said at the end of a פרק
The name of the third פרק of בבא קמא, from its first word

phrases.english: We will return to you, HaMeniach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final resolution in step 10.

steps.title: A new משנה: an ox that gored several oxen, and רבי מאיר's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק opens. When one ox gores four or five oxen one after another, רבי מאיר says the last victim is paid first. Any leftover goes back to the one before him, and so on backward. The last victim comes out best.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: An ox that gored four or five oxen, one after another. The owner pays the last one of them. If there is anything left over, it goes back to the one before him. If there is still something left over, it goes back to the one before that. The very last one gains. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: A brand-new משנה opens a new פרק. It describes an ox that gores several oxen in a row and gives רבי מאיר's order of payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The payment comes out of the goring ox itself, and the ox may not be worth enough to pay everyone. רבי מאיר says to start with the most recent victim and work backward with whatever is left. So the latest victim is the safest, and the earliest victim may end up with nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. This marks the start of the משנה text.
Gored.
One after another.
Leftover. Whatever value remains after paying.
Gains. Comes out ahead.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the first victim is paid first, the way it often works with loans. Here רבי מאיר says it goes the other way: the LAST victim is paid first.

phrases.english: משנה: An ox that gored

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבָּעָה וַחֲמִשָּׁה שְׁוָורִים זֶה אַחַר זֶה –
phrases.english: four or five oxen, one after another,
he pays the last one of them,
and if there is a leftover in it,
it goes back to the one before him,
and if there is still a leftover in it,
it goes back to the one before that,
and each last one is the one who gains;
these are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שׁוֹר שֶׁנָּגַח אַרְבָּעָה וַחֲמִשָּׁה שְׁוָורִים זֶה אַחַר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new פרק right after the הדרן of פרק המניח in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: the last victim is paid first from the goring ox, and any leftover goes back to the earlier victims in reverse order.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's basic case: one goring splits the ox between victim and owner
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון gives a number example. An ox worth 200 kills an ox worth 200, and the dead animal is worth nothing. The victim takes 100 and the owner keeps 100.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: An ox worth 200 gored an ox worth 200, and the carcass is worth nothing. This one takes a מנה, and that one takes a מנה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון starts his own explanation with a simple single-goring case. This sets up the multiple-goring cases that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The damage is 200, and a תם ox pays only half, so 100. The payment comes from the goring ox, which is worth 200. So the victim and the owner each end up with a 100 share of that ox, like two partners.

keyTerms.meaning: Carcass. The dead animal that was killed.
Is worth nothing.
A coin amount equal to 100 זוז (dinars).

phrases.english: רבי שמעון says:
An ox worth two hundred
that gored an ox worth two hundred,
and the carcass is worth nothing,
this one takes a מנה,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the victim. Half of his 200 loss is 100.

phrases.english: and that one takes a מנה.
phrases.notes: "That one" is the owner of the goring ox. He keeps the other 100 of its value.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: שׁוֹר שָׁוֶה מָאתַיִם שֶׁנָּגַח לְשׁוֹר שָׁוֶה מָאתַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי שמעון's alternative way of dividing the money, in contrast to רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After one goring, the victim and the owner each hold 100 of the 200-worth ox.

steps.title: A second goring: the new victim takes 100, and the earlier two get 50 each
steps.stepSummary: The same ox gores another ox worth 200. The new victim takes 100. The first victim and the owner, who shared the ox, are each cut down to 50.
steps.simpleTranslation: It went and gored another ox worth 200. The last one takes a מנה. As for the earlier ones, this one takes 50 זוז and that one takes 50 זוז.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון adds a second goring to his number example and shows how the shares change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new victim is owed half of 200, which is 100, from the ox. That 100 comes out of the shares of everyone who owned the ox, meaning the first victim and the owner. They split the loss equally, so each drops from 100 to 50.

keyTerms.meaning: It went and gored again.
A silver coin, also called a dinar.

phrases.aramaic: חָזַר וְנָגַח שׁוֹר אַחֵר שָׁוֶה מָאתַיִם –
phrases.english: It went and gored another ox worth two hundred:
the last one takes a מנה;
and as for the ones before him:
phrases.notes: This means the two who shared the ox before: the first victim and the owner.

phrases.english: this one takes fifty זוז,
and that one takes fifty זוז.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזַר וְנָגַח שׁוֹר אַחֵר שָׁוֶה מָאתַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the single-goring case by adding a second victim.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After a second goring, the new victim takes 100, and the first victim and the owner each keep 50.

steps.title: A third goring: 100, then 50, then a gold dinar each for the first two
steps.stepSummary: The ox gores a third ox worth 200. The newest victim takes 100. The second victim drops to 50. The first victim and the owner are left with a gold dinar (25) each.
steps.simpleTranslation: It went and gored another ox worth 200. The last one takes a מנה, the one before him takes 50 זוז, and the first two take a gold dinar each.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון finishes his example with a third goring. This shows the pattern: each new victim takes half off the shares of everyone who came before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The newest victim takes 100, and that halves everyone else's share. The second victim goes from 100 to 50. The first victim and the owner go from 50 to 25 each, and 25 silver equals one gold dinar.

keyTerms.meaning: A gold dinar, worth 25 silver dinars.
The first two: the first victim and the owner of the goring ox.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: the last victim is paid first, and any leftover goes backward. רבי שמעון: every victim becomes a partner in the ox, and each new goring cuts every earlier share in half. The numbers come out 100, 50, 25 and 25, adding up to the ox's 200.

phrases.aramaic: חָזַר וְנָגַח שׁוֹר אַחֵר שָׁוֶה מָאתַיִם –
phrases.english: It went and gored another ox worth two hundred:
the last one takes a מנה,
and the one before him takes fifty זוז,
and the first two take a gold dinar each.
phrases.notes: A gold dinar is worth 25 silver ones. So 100 + 50 + 25 + 25 adds up to the full 200.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזַר וְנָגַח שׁוֹר אַחֵר שָׁוֶה מָאתַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same number pattern with a third victim and completes the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After a third goring: the newest victim takes 100, the second takes 50, and the first victim and the owner take 25 (a gold dinar) each.

steps.title: Whose view does the משנה follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking who the author of the משנה is. It claims the משנה fits neither רבי ישמעאל nor רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Who is the author of our משנה? It is not like רבי ישמעאל, and it is not like רבי עקיבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion of the new משנה with a problem: the משנה does not seem to match either of two known opinions. This line sets up the next two steps, which explain why each opinion fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grammatically this is a question, but it works as a challenge. The ending 'not like… and not like…!' means the גמרא already sees a conflict. רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא argued earlier about how a victim relates to the ox that gored. The גמרא assumes the משנה should match one of them.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה begins here
Who is the author of our משנה?
Not in line with (someone's view)

phrases.english: גמרא: Our משנה — whose view is it?
It is not like רבי ישמעאל,
and not like רבי עקיבא!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין מַנִּי? דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, וּדְלָא כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה presented in steps 12–15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The authorship of the משנה about one ox goring several oxen one after another
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's ruling seems to fit neither known opinion about the victim's status, so it is unclear whose view it follows.

steps.title: Why the משנה cannot follow רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל treats victims as creditors. Under that view the first victim should come out best, but the משנה says the last victim does.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל, who says the victims are creditors, why does it say 'the last one gains'? It should have said 'the first one gains'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half of its problem. Under רבי ישמעאל's view, the משנה's ruling would come out backwards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To רבי ישמעאל, a victim is like a lender whose claim is tied to the goring ox. With creditors, the earliest claim gets paid first. So the first victim should be best off. The משנה says the opposite, that the last victim gains.

keyTerms.meaning: Creditors; people who are owed money
Each later victim comes out ahead (the משנה's wording)
Each earlier victim comes out ahead
It should have said

phrases.english: If it follows רבי ישמעאל
who says they are creditors,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the owners of the gored oxen. Each one is owed money from the goring ox.

phrases.english: then why this 'the last one gains'?!
It should have said 'the first one gains'!

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two victims. The משנה says the LAST victim gains. With creditors, you would expect the FIRST victim to gain. That clash is the whole problem.
steps.triggerLanguage: אִי כְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל דְּאָמַר בַּעֲלֵי חוֹבוֹת נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of step 16's challenge: why the משנה cannot be רבי ישמעאל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the last victim gains (אחרון אחרון נשכר)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If victims are creditors, the earliest claim has priority, so the משנה should say the first victim gains.

steps.title: Starting to show why the משנה cannot follow רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds that the victim and the owner are partners in the goring ox. The גמרא starts to quote the משנה's words 'if there is a surplus' to show a problem, and the argument continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the משנה follows רבי עקיבא, who says the ox belongs to partners, then this phrase 'if there is a surplus' —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the second half of its problem: why the משנה does not fit רבי עקיבא either. This line only sets up the challenge; the rest of it comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To רבי עקיבא, once the ox gores, the victim becomes a co-owner of it with the owner. The גמרא picks out the משנה's words 'if there is a surplus,' meaning money left over that goes back to an earlier victim. It is about to explain why that wording doesn't suit a partnership.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox owned by partners
There is a surplus in it; value left over (the משנה's wording)

phrases.english: If it follows רבי עקיבא
who says it is an ox of partners,
phrases.notes: The partners are the owner and the victim. Both share the goring ox, just as in the number example of steps 13–15.

phrases.english: then this 'if there is a surplus' —

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דְּאָמַר תּוֹרָא דְשׁוּתָּפֵי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the second half of step 16's challenge, parallel to step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's wording 'יש בו מותר' (if there is a surplus)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the victim is a partner in the ox, the משנה's surplus wording seems not to fit; the full reasoning continues on the next amud.
